title: Orellana down the Napo and the Amazon, 1541–42
summary: Gonzalo Pizarro's expedition left Quito in early 1541 for the cinnamon country and starved in the forest. In December Orellana went ahead down the Coca and Napo rivers with some fifty men to look for food, built a brigantine, and as the current carried them could not return. They followed the Amazon to the Atlantic, arriving in August 1542, and sailed on to the island of Cubagua. Gaspar de Carvajal, a Dominican on the voyage, wrote an account in which women warriors attacked them, whence the river's name.

events.label: The women warriors
events.source: Francisco de Orellana (Wikipedia); Gaspar de Carvajal (Wikipedia)
events.doubt: Carvajal's chronicle says women led the fighting, and compared them to the Amazons of Greek myth. Later historians think he meant women fighting beside the men, or a classical tale reapplied; his account is the only one.
events.text: Near the mouth of the Trombetas the party fought a people whose women, Carvajal says, fought in front of the men. Orellana called it the river of the Amazons.
